items.title: は (wa) - topic marker
items.explanation: Marks the topic of the sentence - what we are talking about. Written は, pronounced わ.

items.title: です - is / am / are
items.explanation: The polite ending that links a noun to a statement.

items.title: A は B です
items.explanation: The basic sentence pattern: A is B. Japanese often leaves information unstated when context makes it obvious, so it can also mean 'A is in B'.

items.title: を (o) - object marker
items.explanation: Marks the direct object of a verb. Written を, pronounced お.

items.title: に - destination / place
items.explanation: Marks a destination (go to X) or the place where something exists.

items.title: で - place of action
items.explanation: Marks the place where an action happens.

items.title: の - connecting nouns
items.explanation: Connects two nouns: A's B (B of A).

items.title: あります - there is (things)
items.explanation: Used for things that are not alive, and for places.

items.title: ました - polite past
items.pattern: 行きます → 行きました
items.explanation: The polite past tense: 行きます (go) becomes 行きました (went).

items.title: ませんでした - polite past negative
items.pattern: 行きます → 行きませんでした
items.explanation: The polite past negative: 行きませんでした means did not go.

items.title: い-adjectives
items.explanation: Adjectives ending in い (小さい, 美しい) can end a sentence with です.
